Paragraph: "Lengthy are their arms, broad are their eyes and they are the wielders of arrows, bows and swords... and on seeing them, to whom there will be no scare? These two are like the sons of some divinity..."
Situation/Problem_Faced: Formidable appearance of armed strangers intimidating an already hyper-vigilant person.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Sugreeva defends his fear by pointing out the extraordinary physical stature and weaponry of Rama and Lakshmana.
Outcome/Resolution: He explains his rational basis for apprehension.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Tejas (Awe-inspiring divine splendor that induces natural reverence and dread)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The divine presence naturally inspires awe and fear in those who do not yet recognize its benevolent intent.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Visual threat appraisal: calculating risk based on an adversary's physical stature and armament.
